<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>csc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x\tan x - 2(-\csc^2 x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sec x\tan x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>csc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 2\csc^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0 \cdot \sin x - 1 \cdot \cos x}{\sin^2 x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{1}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\csc x\cot x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The numerator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>, which is 1.
options: The Pythagorean identity collapses the numerator to 1.
That identity sets up the quotient; it does not simplify the numerator.

No <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin x\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> appears in the numerator.
That identity rewrites the final answer; the numerator needs the Pythagorean identity.

why.correct: Cotangent, a "co-" function, gets the minus sign; secant does not.
options: Both match the quotient rule results.

The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cot x</annotation></semantics></math> is negative.
Secant is not a "co-" function; its derivative is positive.

Rebuild each from sine and cosine: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>csc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\csc^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x\tan x</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec 0\tan 0 = 1 \cdot 0 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x</annotation></semantics></math> has its lowest point on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left( -\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2} \right)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-\sin x)(\sin x) - (\cos x)(\cos x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\cot x)'</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{-1}{\sin^2 x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>csc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\csc^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Both terms are negative, and they add to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>.

The first term, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-\sin x)(\sin x)</annotation></semantics></math>, is negative.

The second term is subtracted: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\cos^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>, so the terms do not form <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>.

No product <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> survives: each term multiplies a function by itself.
